- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 18-day history shows strong mean reversion, adjust forecast toward historical 30-day average.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay (e.g., 0.5x sentiment weight).
